facts: Goals: AI-enabled city infrastructure (traffic, utilities, public transport), data-driven decisions from city sensor data, automation (traffic, street lighting, energy), better public services (chatbots, predictive maintenance), sustainability (energy, emissions, waste), cyber resilience, and positioning Malaysia as the ASEAN AI-city hub.
Three playbooks published: Digital Avatar for City Data, Digital Twin, Smart Tree Inventory and Risk Monitoring.

Four collaborations announced 18 Sep 2025 at Smart City Expo KL: DNB + Ericsson training programme for council staff (AI, 5G, IoT); DNB + AWS national AI Cities platform (cloud, ML, analytics for real-time urban ops); DNB + MDEC + MSCA frameworks and standards for AI Cities; MDEC + Dell AI Innovation Hub climate-AI testbed in Penang heritage zone.
Support offered to local authorities: engagement, gap resolution, pre-built digital services, showcases, AI Cities network.
name: AI Cities
owner: Ministry of Digital; delivered via MDEC with DNB
status: Active; four collaborations signed Sep 2025, national platform in development
watch: City-data and sensor platforms are high-value targets: watch AI-driven cyberattacks on urban infrastructure
Digital twin / avatar of citizen data must comply with PDPA and the coming AI-PDP Framework

facts: AI Malaysia launched 28 Jul 2026, replacing the National AI Office (NAIO, est. 12 Dec 2024). Mandate: coordinate the National AI Action Plan 2026-2030 (28 initiatives: 14 sector, 14 enablers) and develop governance frameworks, ethical standards, safety testing and red-teaming.

AI Governance Bill consultation paper issued by NAIO on 10 Jul 2026; feedback closed 31 Jul 2026. Proposes a Central AI Authority with Sectoral Leads, 3 risk tiers (Unacceptable / High / Low), Developer vs Deployer duties, 5 principles, mandatory incident reporting (near misses may be reportable) and AI sandboxes.

PDPD consultation on an AI and Personal Data Protection Framework issued 5 Oct 2026; closed 23 Oct 2026. Sets PDPA 2010 compliance duties for AI developers and deployers (lawful basis, DP by design, DPIAs, vendor oversight).
Malaysian AI Safety Institute will sit under AI Malaysia. Target: AI Nation by 2030.

status: AI Governance Bill in consultation; target completion end-2026

facts: MY-AISafe contributes to E12 (AI Trust Function): create an AI evaluation, assessment and response capability so Malaysia can pre-empt and manage AI risks.
E12 functions: Standards & Policy; Evaluation & Certification; Incident Monitoring & Forensics; International Collaboration & Capacity Building.

Post-release duties named in the overview: Incident management (receive, assess and contain AI incidents and near-misses, then share what was learned) and Threat intelligence (track emerging AI risks and misuse patterns, give early warning before they spread).

Three workstreams: AI RDCI (safety evals, testing, red teaming); Strategic collaboration (local and international partners, talent); AI Assurance, Standards & Evaluation (benchmarks, test protocols, assurance).
Responsible AI test areas follow AIGE 2024 principles: fairness, reliability, safety & control, privacy & security, inclusiveness, transparency, accountability, human benefit.
Timeline: AIGE Sep 2024; NAIO Dec 2024; AI Governance Bill consultation 10-31 Jul 2026; AI Malaysia + MY-AISafe 28 Jul 2026; Bill tabling targeted 2027.
goal: E12 target: establish a rapid and reliable national capability to detect, assess and contain critical AI-related incidents. This channel is the live detect-and-early-warning layer for that target.
name: AI Safety
owner: Malaysia AI Safety Institute (MY-AISafe), under AI Malaysia / Kementerian Digital
status: Announced 28 Jul 2026 with AI Malaysia. Delivers E12 AI Trust Function of the National AI Action Plan 2026-2030
watch: How this channel maps to E12: Detect = 3-hourly scanner; Assess = severity scoring (1-5 impact once the RAID link is added); Contain = status workflow New -> Acknowledged -> Monitoring -> Closed; Share learnings = Closed items with notes.
Overview gives no reporting channels, procedures, SLAs or KPIs for incident management yet: define them (e.g. acknowledge Critical within 1 scan cycle = 3 h).
